body: Communities can pass knowledge and expression through storytelling, song and performance. Words, melody, rhythm, movement and the relationships among participants can all matter. A story may take different forms when told at different times or by different people.

A recording can preserve one event. It can lose the ways people learn a performance, collaborate in it or decide when it is appropriate. In the UNESCO convention on living heritage, communities and practitioners have roles in identifying and safeguarding their practices. A record about one tradition needs its own context.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: The archive contains a photograph of one dance performance and a record of one musical instrument. These visual objects convey limited information about rhythm, sound and community meaning.
purpose: Explain how oral performance transmits knowledge and changes across occasions.

terms.definition: Knowledge or expression passed between people through spoken language or forms such as songs and stories.
An enacted expression that can combine movement, sound, speech, objects or audience participation.

title: Oral traditions and performance
